keyframe_review.note: 321,604 km2 is Paraguay as it claimed itself, not its settled land: by the gazetteer 696 cells in modern Paraguay, 337 in Mato Grosso do Sul north of the Apa and 317 in Formosa south of the Pilcomayo. The Paraguayan War page calls those 'the disputed territories north of the Apa River' and 'all the disputed lands south of the Pilcomayo River now constituting Formosa Province', and says the war cost Paraguay 'about 140,000 square kilometres' (30 to 40% of the territory it claimed before the war), so the shape is within a factor of two of the page figures. The modern infobox gives 406,752 km2 (ratio 0.79). Treat the edges as claims (soft). No page opened dates the claim in 1811.
322,598 km2, the same outline within 1,000 km2. The page says Francia 'ruled Paraguay from 1814 until his death in 1840'; it gives nothing on borders in this period.
321,604 km2, the 1811 outline again; unverified: page budget. The page gives no border event for 1820-1821.

321,933 km2 to 1864, the prewar claim. Unverified for the years before the war: the Paraguay page says only that 'Fortifications were built, especially along the Apa River and in Gran Chaco' under Carlos Antonio López and that independence was 'Recognized: 25 November 1842'. The Paraguayan War page gives the claimed outline's loss, which fixes its edges: north of the Apa, south of the Pilcomayo, Misiones.

382,793 km2, the prewar outline plus the 1865 conquests: Mato Grosso ('invading the Brazilian province of Mato Grosso on 14 December 1864', Corumbá in January 1865), Corrientes ('took the city with 3,000 men' on 13 April 1865) and São Borja (12 June 1865). By the gazetteer the shape has 542 cells in Mato Grosso do Sul, 21 in Corrientes and some in Rio Grande do Sul. The conquests are drawn as the occupation events of the ledger (hatched). fx-34 (F295): the 1865 shape put 205 cells of Mato Grosso do Sul and 34 of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazilian land the Paraguayans occupied, in Paraguay's own outline, while the ledger (/4, /6) and the empire-of-brazil dossier (keyframe _1865, ledger /21-/23) carry them as occupation of Brazil's land; the size rule then gave them to Paraguay. Subtracted: Brazil outside the 345-cell strip north of the Apa, which Paraguay held before the war. The Corrientes cells (occupation /5, argentine side) are not touched here.

notes:
WHAT THE SHAPES ARE. Cliopatria draws Paraguay at 321,604-321,933 km2 from 1811 to 1864: modern Paraguay east of the river plus claimed land north of the Apa (Mato Grosso do Sul, 337 cells) and south of the Pilcomayo (Formosa, 317 cells). The Paraguayan War page calls those 'the disputed territories', so the early shapes are claims (soft), and the 1872 and 1876 losses are losses of claims. Cliopatria has no shape for 1870-1876 (occupation) and none of the Chaco before 1936.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The 1868-1869 shape (38,439 km2) is the south that the Allies overran; I read it as the occupied zone and redraw the state as modern Paraguay, but the pages do not say what López's government controlled month by month (the hills northeast of Asunción, then Cerro Corá). (2) Allied occupation: the page gives Brazil's capture of Asunción on 1 January 1869 and the occupation 'until 1876', and says 'Argentine and Brazilian troops'; the ledger records Brazil only, with the same land. (3) When the last Mato Grosso districts and Corrientes were lost: the pages give Corumbá (June 1867) and Corrientes ('subsequent months' after September 1865), and the years in the ledger are conf 1. (4) The Hayes award region is approximated by Presidente Hayes Department; the Paraguayan War page gives only 'between the Río Verde and the main Pilcomayo branch'. (5) The Chaco Boreal: the Chaco War page gives no pre-war control, no date for the Hayes award, and no 1938 treaty date (the July 1938 conference only); who held what in the Chaco north of the award before 1932 is unknown, and Bolivia's side belongs to the 'bolivia' dossier (another part). (6) The Triple Alliance Treaty (1 May 1865), the Treaty of Loizaga-Cotegipe and the Machaín-Irigoyen Treaty have their own pages that were not opened; a gap-filler could date the claimed lines. (7) Misiones: the Cliopatria 1822 shape has almost none of Argentine Misiones, though the page says the disputed lands that 'definitively became' Misiones were Paraguay's claim.

OCCUPATION ROLES. The ledger uses occupation_start/end for Paraguay's own conquests (counterparts empire-of-brazil, argentine-confederation, as occupier) and for the Allied occupation of Paraguay (counterpart empire-of-brazil, roles reversed, from the owner's side). The 'empire-of-brazil' and 'argentine-confederation' dossiers (another part) should carry the mirror events.

DISAGREEMENTS. Humaitá: the page says 25 July 1868. The page gives both 'almost 40%' and 'approximately 30 percent' for the war's loss. The 52,000 km2 of the Chaco division does not match three quarters of 600,000 km2. The Paraguay page's departments table totals 406,796 km2 against the infobox's 406,752.

RULERS. The Paraguay page gives dated rulers only in fragments (Francia 1814-1840; López from 1841; Solano López from 1862; Franco 1936; Morínigo 1940-1948; Stroessner 1954-1989; Rodríguez 1989), not a list; none is recorded.

GAZETTEER. Every name resolved (Asunción, Ñeembucú, Presidente Hayes, Boquerón, Alto Paraguay, Formosa, Misiones, Corrientes, Rio Grande do Sul).
